title: Internal extension of the rational polynomial bar contraction
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] equipped with a unital ring homomorphism $\mathbf Q\to A(*)$. Use internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], their ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $r\geq0$. In degree $n\geq0$ let $P_{A,r}^n$ be the internal direct sum of $A$ indexed by monomials in the $nr$ variables $x_{a,i}$ ($1\leq a\leq n$, $1\leq i\leq r$), with monomials as in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Its differential is
$$(df)(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1})=f(x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1})+\sum_{a=1}^{n}(-1)^a f(x_1,\ldots,x_a+x_{a+1},\ldots,x_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(x_1,\ldots,x_n).$$
Let $K_{A,r}=\bigoplus_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}}A[-|I|]$ have zero differential, and put both complexes zero in negative degrees. Define $i_A(e_\varnothing)=1$ and $i_A(e_{\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}})=x_{1,i_1}\cdots x_{q,i_q}$.

Take any rational contraction $(i_{\mathbf Q},p_{\mathbf Q},h_{\mathbf Q})$ with the monomial formulas and finite-support property of [lem-sfb-rational-polynomial-bar-contraction]. Extend $p_{\mathbf Q}$ and $h_{\mathbf Q}$ on each monomial by the same finite rational coefficients, multiplied by the coefficient section of $A$. These prescriptions define internal $A$-linear maps $p_A:P_{A,r}\to K_{A,r}$ and $h_A^q:P_{A,r}^q\to P_{A,r}^{q-1}$, natural under every profinite restriction. They satisfy
$$di_A=0,\quad p_Ad=0,\quad p_Ai_A=1,\quad dh_A+h_Ad=1-i_Ap_A.$$
Thus the specified $i_A$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and an isomorphism $K_{A,r}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{A,r}$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$, with inverse induced by $p_A$. This holds for the zero ring and for $r=0$, where $i_A$ is the degree-zero constant inclusion. The prescriptions involve finite sums only; there is no completeness or flatness hypothesis on $A$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-size-convention], work with a small representative of the coherent profinite site in the chosen coefficient universe. Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] with $R=A$ (and trivial groups): its explicit assertion that $\mathcal M_A$ is Grothendieck abelian, together with [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], supplies the small coproducts and additive category used below. Let $J_n$ be the set of all monomials in the $nr$ variables of $P^n$ (with no bound on polynomial total degree) and $E_n$ the set of $n$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,r\}$. Write their coproduct injections as $\iota_j:A\to P^n$ and $\kappa_I:A\to K^n$. By [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], maps out of either coproduct are uniquely specified on these injections. In particular, equality on every injection proves equality of internal module maps.

source.place: Tag 002F, definition-colimit, plus the explicitly cited condensed-module infrastructure

proof.text: Write $c_S$ for the restriction of the image of $c\in\mathbf Q$ in $A(*)$ to a profinite set $S$. Multiplication $a\mapsto c_Sa$ on $A(S)$ is additive, commutes with restrictions, and commutes with the regular $A$-action, since $A$ is commutative. Internally this is $s_c=\mu\circ(c\otimes1_A)\circ\lambda_A^{-1}$, where $c:\mathbf1\to A$ is the constant section. Associativity and commutativity of $\mu$ give $s_c\mu=\mu(1_A\otimes s_c)$, the action-commuting condition of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Thus $s_c$ is an internal $A$-linear endomorphism of the regular module. On sections, $s_{c+c'}=s_c+s_{c'}$, $s_{cc'}=s_cs_{c'}$ and $s_1=1$. These are sheaf-map equalities because the underlying maps agree on every $S$. No injectivity of $\mathbf Q\to A(*)$ is used.

proof.text: For any of the given rational maps $T$, write its value on a basis vector as $T(e_j)=\sum_{k\in F_j}t_{kj}e_k$, with $F_j$ finite. Define $T_A$ by $T_A\iota_j=\sum_{k\in F_j}\iota_k s_{t_{kj}}$, using the appropriate $\kappa$ injections for $K$. The coproduct universal property makes this an internal map; each prescribed summand is already internal-linear. Apply this to $p_{\mathbf Q}$ and $h_{\mathbf Q}$, whose finite support is part of [lem-sfb-rational-polynomial-bar-contraction], and to $i_{\mathbf Q}$ and $d_{\mathbf Q}$. The ordered inclusion has a single coefficient $1$ on each $e_I$, so its extension is the specified $i_A$. Each coface substitution in $d$ expands a monomial into a finite sum with integer coefficients; hence its extension is precisely the displayed differential. On a coefficient section $a\in A(S)$ the formula is $a\mapsto\sum_k(t_{kj})_S a\,e_k$, which is the required prescription and commutes with every restriction $S'\to S$. This construction does not identify sections of a coproduct with a sectionwise direct sum.

proof.text:
The extension preserves sums and composition. Indeed, on the $j$-th injection, if $U(e_j)=\sum_{\ell\in F_j}u_{\ell j}e_\ell$ and $V(e_\ell)=\sum_{k\in G_\ell}v_{k\ell}e_k$, then
$$V_AU_A\iota_j=\sum_{\ell\in F_j}\sum_{k\in G_\ell}\iota_k s_{v_{k\ell}u_{\ell j}}=(VU)_A\iota_j.$$
Both sums are finite, and $c\mapsto s_c$ preserves addition and multiplication by step 2. The same computation for addition and for the identity, followed by equality on coproduct injections, proves the assertion. Apply it to the rational identities of [lem-sfb-rational-polynomial-bar-contraction]: it gives $d_A^2=0$, $d_Ai_A=0$, $p_Ad_A=0$, $p_Ai_A=1$ and $d_Ah_A+h_Ad_A=1-i_Ap_A$ in each degree, including degree zero with the negative-degree maps zero. Thus these are genuine complexes and the displayed maps and homotopy have exactly the required signs and degrees.

proof.text: The identities just proved say that $p_A$ is a chain inverse to $i_A$ up to the stated chain homotopy: one composite is exactly $1_K$ and the other is homotopic to $1_P$. In the homotopy category they therefore become inverse morphisms. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $D(\mathcal M_A)$ is equivalently the localization of that homotopy category at quasi-isomorphisms, so the images of $i_A,p_A$ remain inverse; this proves the asserted derived isomorphism, with its specified map. If $A$ is the zero ring every regular module and its coproducts are zero and all formulas still hold. If $r=0$, $E_0$ is a singleton and $E_n$ is empty for $n>0$, while every $J_n$ consists of the constant monomial: $d^n=0$ for even $n$ and $d^n=1$ for odd $n$. The construction gives the constant inclusion in degree zero and the supplied rational homotopy still satisfies the identities after extension. For $n>r$, $E_n$ is empty and $K^n=0$. Only finite sums on each source summand have occurred; no infinite summation, completeness, exact scalar extension or flatness is invoked.
